text:
aj: Heads up — canary perf gate tripped on the release we merged this morning (commit abc123). p95 latency +18% on small-seq workload and throughput down ~12%. Holding rollout. :exclamation:

maria: saw the alert. CI perf job 0702 failed too with noisy results, but the canary numbers are real. Can someone grab a flamegraph? :eyes:

dev-bot: CI perf-run-0702 summary: p50 +5%, p95 +18%, start/end: 2026-03-17T11:02Z. Benchmark: smallseq-kv-heavy. Repro rate: 3/5 runs.

chris: quick repro locally on a 3090 clone with the smallseq harness. Attaching perf profile output (trimmed):
```
- user time dominated by kernel_selector::choose_path
- increased calls into quantized_attention_kernel_v2 by ~40%
- batcher shows more single-request batches (avg batch size down from 4.2 -> 2.9)
```

linh: that smells like the kernel selection change in PR #4126 where we added a heuristic to prefer quantized kernels for length<=64. It was trying to optimize long-running cases but maybe it's flipping too early and causing worse latency for batched small sequences.

sam: also noticed higher KV cache evictions in that same run — eviction rate spiked when batcher shrank. My theory: kernel change changes latency/exec time distribution, batcher backs off and we lose KV reuse, causing more recompute of KV and increasing total work.

eric: +1. I ran a run with kvcache metrics on and saw write-through misses go up ~30%. That would amplify p95.

aj: can we confirm whether it's the kernel selector heuristic or the quantized kernel quality/regress? Chris, can you run with kernel_selector=v1 (pre-4126) and v2 side-by-side?

chris: doing that now. quick diff: toggling selector to v1 in a canary build made p95 go back down to expected — p95 delta ~+2% vs baseline. So selector change is the likely root cause.

maria: good catch. So immediate mitigation: revert the selector heuristic in canary and roll that back while we fix. Is that low-risk?

aj: I prefer a targeted revert of the heuristic only (not the whole kernel routing infra). Please open a rollback PR with description + perf numbers. Also add a canary hold flag so we don't propagate.

chris: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/serving/commit/revert-4126 (WIP). I'll add benchmark diffs.

dev-bot: deploy-canary job queued. Status: pending approval from @aj.

aj: approved, go ahead. We also need to harden our perf tests to catch this class earlier — current smallseq-kv-heavy bench is flaky (3/5). We should: 
- add deterministic seeding and fixed load generator host labels
- increase runs and median+90 reporting
- add a threshold check on kv_eviction_rate + p95 not just p50
- add a synthetic sample that biases toward mixed-length sequences so selector heuristics get exercised

linh: I can own the test changes. Plan: (1) make harness deterministic, (2) add a new benchmark suite smallseq-mixed-kv with 10 runs and require p95 within 5% and kv_eviction_rate < 5%. I'll push changes and a patch to the CI thresholds config.

sam: also propose we add a smoke profiling step to release jobs that grabs a short perf trace and validates kernel selection distribution hasn't shifted >10% from baseline. That would catch heuristics flips.

maria: agreed. Let's also add an alerting rule that looks at batcher average size drop and kv_eviction spikes during canary — hold if both exceed thresholds.

eric: note: some quantized kernels have slightly different latency variance, so tests need to be robust to small p50 noise. That's why I like adding kv_eviction_rate and batch-size checks as they capture second-order effects.

aj: timeline: rollback now, canary redeploy in 15m. Linh, get bench changes into CI by EOD. Sam, add smoke profiler step as follow-up PR. Maria, update runbook for canary perf hold to include kv_eviction metric.

chris: rollback applied to canary, monitoring. Early numbers look back to baseline on p95. Fingers crossed. :crossed_fingers:

dev-bot: canary-deploy-1845509930 completed. Post-deploy perf-run queued.

srebot: monitoring note: KV eviction alert threshold breached earlier; currently within normal after rollback. Will keep 1h watch.

maria: thanks everyone. We'll do a postmortem tomorrow in the perf retro backlog and include the new CI test items. Please add short notes to the ticket: PERF-789 (root cause: kernel-selector heuristic misfire; mitigation: revert + test hardening).

aj: closing the thread here. Good incident response — quick rollback and clear follow-ups.
